high.title: BNP Paribas Raises South Korea Terminal Rate Forecast to 3.25% After Monetary Policy Board Meeting
high.summary:
BNP Paribas has revised upward its terminal rate forecast for the Bank of Korea (BOK) from 3.00% to 3.25%, following the Monetary Policy Board's decision on July 16th to raise the base rate by 25 basis points to 2.75%. BNP Paribas economist Yoon Ji-ho cited continued upside surprises in economic indicators and higher-than-expected, prolonged inflationary pressures as the key drivers behind the revised terminal rate projection. This is a significant development for KRW and Korean government bond (KTB) markets. A higher terminal rate implies a more hawkish BOK policy path than previously anticipated, which could provide KRW with upside support as the interest rate differential with major currencies potentially narrows. For KTB investors, the upward revision signals further potential selling pressure on the short-to-medium end of the yield curve as markets reprice the rate path higher. Fund managers should monitor upcoming inflation prints and BOK communications closely, as any additional hawkish signals could accelerate KTB yield rises and reinforce KRW strength. This development warrants a reassessment of duration positioning in Korean fixed income portfolios.

---

high.title: Dollar-Won Closes Higher at 1,486.00 Amid Ongoing U.S.-Iran Conflict
high.summary: The dollar-won exchange rate closed sharply higher at 1,486.00 won in the New York session, representing a 7.50 won gain from the previous Seoul market close of 1,478.50 won. The move was driven primarily by escalating U.S.-Iran military confrontation, which is fueling broad risk-off sentiment and safe-haven demand for the U.S. dollar. The 4.00 won rise versus the prior New York close further confirms sustained dollar buying pressure rather than a one-session spike. For KRW traders, the 1,480–1,490 range is now the critical zone to monitor. A sustained break above 1,490 could trigger accelerated stop-loss selling of KRW, while also raising the probability of Bank of Korea (BOK) smoothing operations. The geopolitical risk premium embedded in KRW is likely to persist as long as the U.S.-Iran conflict remains active. Bond investors should watch for any safe-haven flows into Korean government bonds that could partially offset KRW weakness. The key risk event to watch is whether the conflict broadens, which could push oil prices further and compound Korea's import cost burden, widening the trade deficit and adding further downward pressure on KRW.

high.title: NDF at 1,487.00/1,487.30 Won — Up 9.50 Won from Spot Close
high.summary: The dollar-won one-month NDF rose sharply overnight in the New York market, last quoted at a mid-rate of 1,487.15 won. Adjusted for the one-month swap point of -0.85 won, this represents a 9.50 won premium over the previous Seoul spot close of 1,478.50 won — a notably large overnight move signaling strong risk-off positioning. The bid/ask spread of 1,487.00/1,487.30 indicates relatively tight liquidity conditions, suggesting the move is directional rather than illiquid. For KRW traders, the NDF level is a critical leading indicator for the Seoul opening rate. A 9.50 won implied gap-up points to an opening well above 1,486–1,487, which could test the BOK's tolerance for rapid won depreciation. This level also approaches the psychologically and technically significant 1,490 threshold. If offshore NDF positioning continues to build on the short-KRW side overnight, the Seoul session on July 18 is likely to open defensively, with the risk of BOK smoothing intervention increasing materially. Fund managers with long KRW exposure should reassess hedging ratios ahead of the Seoul open.

high.title: [Bond Market - Weekly] Escalating Middle East Conflict and Q2 GDP in Focus - Gauging Consecutive Rate Hikes
high.summary: South Korea's bond market is bracing for a cautious week (July 20–24) as two key risk factors converge: the release of Q2 GDP data and sharply escalating US-Iran military tensions. The GDP print will be critical in calibrating BOK rate expectations — a weaker-than-expected reading could reinforce the case for a pause or cut, while resilient growth would keep the door open for further tightening. Simultaneously, the geopolitical shock in the Middle East — with two US soldiers reportedly killed in Jordan — has injected fresh risk-off sentiment into regional bond markets. For Korean government bond (KTB) traders, the key tension is between domestic macro data pointing toward a dovish pivot and external inflationary pressure from surging oil prices, which could force the BOK's hand. Watch the short-end of the KTB curve for repricing of rate expectations following the GDP release, and monitor any BOK communication for guidance on consecutive rate hike probability. A widening of the KRW/USD spread on risk aversion is also plausible if Middle East tensions escalate further.

high.title: US-Iran Conflict Escalates - Markets Eye Oil Price Impact on Interest Rates
high.summary: Military escalation between the US and Iran is sending shockwaves through global financial markets, with Strait of Hormuz vessel traffic collapsing by 92% — from over 100 ships to just eight as of July 17th, according to shipping intelligence firm Kpler. This represents a critical supply bottleneck for global oil flows, with direct implications for Korean inflation dynamics. Korea is one of Asia's most oil-import-dependent economies, meaning a sustained oil price spike would feed directly into domestic CPI, complicate the BOK's rate path, and exert depreciation pressure on the KRW via a deteriorating trade balance. Bond markets face a stagflationary risk scenario: higher inflation argues against rate cuts, while global growth fears from a supply shock argue for easing. For KRW traders, sustained oil above $90–95/bbl would likely trigger meaningful won weakness, particularly if the current account surplus narrows. Watch Brent crude as the key leading indicator for both KTB yield direction and USD/KRW trajectory this week. Any diplomatic de-escalation would likely see a sharp reversal rally in KRW and a bull steepening of the KTB curve.

high.title: [New York Foreign Exchange Market - Weekly] ECB Meeting Amid Middle East Tensions - Will September Hike Remain on the Table?
high.summary: The New York FX market this week is expected to remain highly sensitive to central bank positioning in the context of surging oil prices. The ECB is widely expected to hold rates but market focus will be on forward guidance — specifically whether September and December hike bets remain intact given the oil-driven inflation resurgence. For KRW, the secondary implications are significant: a more hawkish ECB tone would support EUR and broadly pressure the USD, offering some relief to Asian EM currencies including KRW. Conversely, if central banks signal concern about growth headwinds from an oil shock, risk-off positioning would likely favor the USD and pressure KRW. Indonesia's anticipated rate hike — reportedly a cumulative 100bps over two months — also highlights the aggressive tightening posture across EM Asia, creating a regional rate divergence context in which the BOK's next move will be closely scrutinized. New Zealand CPI data is also on the radar as a proxy for developed-market inflation trends. FX traders should monitor EUR/USD as a key directional signal for the broader USD index and its pass-through to USD/KRW this week.

high.title: [FX-Weekly] 'Exporter Dollar Sales vs Mideast Tensions' - Searching for Direction Around 1,480 Won
high.summary:
The Seoul FX market is entering the week with competing directional forces, making for a complex trading environment around the 1,480 KRW/USD level. On the supply side, dollar-selling pressure is expected from SK Hynix's ADR proceeds conversion and forward contract sales from heavy industry exporters — both of which are meaningful structural flows that could cap USD/KRW upside. However, this is being offset by a fresh risk-off catalyst: renewed U.S.-Iran military confrontation, which is driving safe-haven demand for the dollar and creating upward pressure on the pair.

Critically, the Bank of Korea's Monetary Policy Board last week raised the base rate by 25 basis points, moving from 2.50% to 2.75%. This is a hawkish signal that could provide medium-term support for the KRW by narrowing the interest rate differential with the Fed, though near-term FX direction remains hostage to geopolitical developments.

medium.title: Next Week's Schedule of Bank of Korea, Financial Services Commission, and Financial Supervisory Service
medium.summary: The BOK's weekly schedule reveals several market-relevant events. On Monday July 20th, the BOK will release its Bank Lending Survey Results covering Q2 2026 trends and Q3 2026 outlook — a key read on credit conditions and domestic demand that could influence rate expectations. BOK Governor Shin Hyun-song is scheduled to attend the 31st EMEAP Governors' Meeting and the 15th EMEAP Central Bank Governors and Heads of Financial Supervisory Authorities Meeting on Tuesday July 21st, which may yield commentary on regional monetary coordination and FX stability. Additionally, a BOK Issue Note on "Why Is This Terms of Trade Improvement Different — Real Economic Impact of Semiconductor Industry Boom" was released Sunday, potentially informing the BOK's macro narrative around growth and inflation. Traders should watch the lending survey for signs of credit tightening or loosening that could influence the BOK's forward guidance.

medium.title: Next Week's Schedule for Ministry of Finance and Economy and Other Economic Ministries
medium.summary: The Ministry of Finance and Economy schedule for the week of July 20–26 highlights a busy policy calendar with potential macro implications. On Monday July 20th, the Deputy Prime Minister will chair the 271st Foreign Economic Ministers' Meeting, which could address trade, FX, or external economic policy developments relevant to KRW dynamics. A Cabinet Meeting is scheduled for Tuesday July 21st, along with the Korea Strategic Economy Forum Part II, where fiscal and economic strategy discussions may occur. Market participants should monitor any official statements emerging from the Foreign Economic Ministers' Meeting, particularly any signals on currency policy, trade posture, or external sector management that could influence KRW sentiment during the week.

medium.title: WTI Surges 4.5% as U.S. Deploys Additional Aerial Refueling Tankers in Iran Escalation
medium.summary:
WTI crude surged $3.54 (4.48%) to $82.49 per barrel as the U.S.-Iran military conflict intensified, with the U.S. deploying additional aerial refueling tankers in a sign of escalation preparedness. For Korea — a major oil importer — a sustained oil price spike above $80/barrel materially worsens the terms of trade, pressures the current account, and adds imported inflationary stress that complicates BOK monetary policy. Higher energy import costs directly widen Korea's trade deficit, reducing the current account surplus that has historically acted as a structural support for KRW. Bond investors should note that sustained oil-driven inflation could keep the BOK on hold longer than currently priced, limiting the near-term scope for rate cuts and capping any rally in Korean government bonds. This oil price development reinforces the bearish near-term KRW view established by the NDF and spot FX moves above.

---

medium.title: Semiconductor Investment Poses Limited Debt Threat as Growth Prospects Brighten Credit Environment
medium.summary:
While primarily a credit market story, this article carries marginal relevance for Korean bond investors. Analysts note that South Korea's semiconductor majors — unlike U.S. hyperscalers — are financing their capital expenditure cycles through equity and retained earnings rather than bond issuance, limiting supply-side pressure on the domestic Korean corporate bond market. This is a modest positive for KTB and Korean credit spreads, as it reduces the risk of crowding-out effects or yield widening driven by heavy corporate issuance. The semiconductor-driven growth outlook is also seen improving the broader credit environment, potentially supporting risk appetite in Korean fixed income. Bond investors should monitor whether this dynamic shifts if semiconductor capex accelerates further and companies eventually turn to debt markets. For KRW traders, a stronger semiconductor growth narrative is broadly supportive of the won via improved current account and export earnings expectations.

---

medium.title: Iraqi PM to Visit Iran Soon in Effort to Ease US-Iran Tensions
medium.summary:
Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi is set to visit Tehran in a diplomatic bid to ease US-Iran tensions, according to Iran's semi-official Mehr News Agency. While this is a geopolitical rather than a directly financial story, its market relevance lies in its potential to serve as an early de-escalation signal. For Korean bond and FX markets, any credible diplomatic progress could quickly reverse the risk-off premium currently being priced into KRW and KTBs. Traders positioned for further oil-driven KRW weakness should treat this as a key tail risk to monitor — a successful diplomatic intervention could trigger a sharp short-covering rally in KRW. At this stage, the diplomatic effort remains preliminary and unconfirmed in scope, so the base case for elevated geopolitical risk pricing remains intact.

---

medium.title: US Military Reports 2 Soldiers Killed, 1 Missing in Iranian Missile Attack
medium.summary:
US Central Command confirmed that two American service members were killed and one is missing following Iranian ballistic missile and drone attacks in Jordan, with four additional soldiers hospitalized and subsequently discharged. This represents a significant escalation in U.S.-Iran military tensions and is the primary geopolitical risk factor flagged in the FX-Weekly outlook (Article 1) as a driver of risk-off sentiment in Asian FX markets. For KRW traders, Middle East escalation historically pressures the won through safe-haven USD buying and elevated oil price risk — Korea being a major energy importer. Bond investors should monitor any flight-to-quality dynamics and their effect on Korean sovereign spreads. Watch for further U.S. military responses or Iranian retaliation that could amplify volatility.
